task:
Assess RISK-24 for the planned pilot in roughly 180-280 words: give the supported risk/control conclusion, next actions, and reopening triggers. This is an output-only assessment; supplied facts are authoritative. Do not investigate, implement, or approve deployment.

The pilot sends 200 confidential client reports in one batch. A known possible mapper failure assigns reports to the wrong client. Project policy rates any external cross-client disclosure HIGH impact. Its occurrence frequency is unknown. Dispatch is irreversible: sent reports cannot be recalled. Restoring the database does not remove copies already delivered.

At candidate c18, generated reports stay in a hold queue until a fixed dispatch time measured from generation start. The detector covers every misassignment produced by this specific mapper failure before release. EV-41 at the pilot's exact load/configuration verified an alarm within 45 seconds of generation start, delivery to on-call and acknowledgement within a further 30 seconds, and stop-and-purge completing within a further 45 seconds. This chain uses independent infrastructure that remains available during the mapper failure; purge removes all queued reports and prevents later delivery. No report can dispatch before the hold expires. All these guarantees apply to this pilot; they do not cover other failure modes or expanded load.

The current hold is 90 seconds. GAP-06 records existing Operations acceptance of this 200-report pilot only while the verified stop-and-purge chain completes strictly before dispatch, with an on-call responder assigned. That responder is assigned; the acceptance is otherwise current. No pilot has run.

The delivery lead calls the risk eliminated because a database restore is available and says no further tracking is useful. Operations owns the chain and its drill evidence; the product owner controls pilot scope. Address that claim and whether GAP-06 still applies without inventing a new approval policy.
